newsitem.title: USA: US High Court allows state income tax on hospitals.
newsitem.headline: US High Court allows state income tax on hospitals.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court Monday upheld a New York state law that taxes the income of hospitals run by employee welfare benefit plans.

The high court, by a 7-2 vote, said the federal Employee Retirement Income Security Act does not preclude the state from imposing a gross receipts tax on medical centers funded under the law, which governs employee welfare benefit plans.
"We hold that New York may collect its tax," Justice John Paul Stevens declared for the court majority.

In the case, a fund that administers a plan for two unions challeged the law. The fund, which operates three medical centers for union members, argued that the New York provision indirectly taxes health benefits.
The ruling was a victory for the state, which argued the tax affects benefits indirectly and does not violate the federal law.

The ruling also was a victory for the federal government, which said the tax applies generally, operates in an area of traditional state regulation and does not directly "relate to" the benefits plans, as required by the federal law.
